Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Ledbetter
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 04/05/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 566 as introduced would, beginning October 1, 2021, (1) increase the annual transfer of sales tax discount receipts to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) for capital outlay, repairs, and maintenance of the state parks system from $5 million, currently, to $7.5 million and (2) would correspondingly decrease sales tax discount receipts that would otherwise have been credited to the State General Fund by $2.5 million.
Further, this bill provides that beginning with fiscal year 2023, the State Treasurer shall annually adjust the $7.5 million credited to DCNR to reflect the change in the Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers (CPI-U), which would increase the amount credited to DCNR by an estimated $125,000 annually dependent upon the actual CPI-U adjustment and likewise decrease the amount that otherwise would have been credited to the State General Fund.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Date: 04/19/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 566 as passed the House of Representatives would, beginning October 1, 2021, (1) increase the annual transfer of sales tax discount receipts to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) for capital outlay, repairs, and maintenance of the state parks system from $5 million, currently, to $6.5 million and (2) would correspondingly decrease sales tax discount receipts that would otherwise have been credited to the State General Fund by $1.5 million.
Further, this bill provides that beginning with fiscal year 2023, the State Treasurer shall annually adjust the $6.5 million credited to DCNR to reflect the change in the Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers (CPI-U), which would increase the amount credited to DCNR by an estimated $110,000 annually dependent upon the actual CPI-U adjustment and likewise decrease the amount that otherwise would have been credited to the State General Fund.
Greg Albritton, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation General Fund

Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund
Sponsor: Ledbetter
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 04/20/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 566 as passed the House of Representatives would, beginning October 1, 2021, (1) increase the annual transfer of sales tax discount receipts to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) for capital outlay, repairs, and maintenance of the state parks system from $5 million, currently, to $6.5 million and (2) would correspondingly decrease sales tax discount receipts that would otherwise have been credited to the State General Fund by $1.5 million.
Further, this bill provides that beginning with fiscal year 2023, the State Treasurer shall annually adjust the $6.5 million credited to DCNR to reflect the change in the Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers (CPI-U), which would increase the amount credited to DCNR by an estimated $110,000 annually dependent upon the actual CPI-U adjustment and likewise decrease the amount that otherwise would have been credited to the State General Fund.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation General Fund, this bill would change the transfer amount to DCNR from $6.5 million to $7 million, which would simultaneously decrease the sales tax discount receipts that would have been credited to the State General Fund from $1.5 million to $2 million.
Additionally, the $7 million credited to DCNR will increase the estimated annual CPI adjustment from $110,000 to $116,000 annually.
Greg Albritton, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation General Fund
